items.title: PhD Student Vacancy. DeepSoil: Integrated Soil Hydrological Assessment with CPT–ML for Flood & Drought Risk Screening
items.desc: Climate change is bringing more intense rainfall and periods of drought to Scotland, putting increasing pressure on farms, soils and water resources. How can we identify land that is most vulnerable to flooding or water shortages before damage occurs? The answer may lie beneath our feet. Most soil assessments focus on the surface, yet deeper layers can strongly influence how quickly water enters the ground, how much it stores and how it moves during wet and dry periods. DeepSoil will investigate these hidden processes by combining field measurements, soil laboratory analysis, machine learning […] and spatial modelling. This 3.5 year PhD is a joint project between the James Hutton Institute and Abertay University. The successful candidate will work at two contrasting research sites: the Centre for Sustainable Cropping at Balruddery, where regenerative and conventional management practices can be compared, and the Glensaugh Climate-Positive Farming Initiative, representing upland farming conditions. The student will use Cone Penetration Testing (CPT), a technique that measures soil resistance and related properties through the soil profile, alongside soil cores and laboratory tests. Together, these observations will help develop and validate two project-defined indicators: infiltration capacity (I*), describing how readily soil can take in water, and storage potential (S*), describing its capacity to retain water. Using machine learning, geostatistics and environmental datasets, the student will turn field observations into high-resolution maps, targeting approximately 10 m resolution at field scale and 25 m at catchment scale. Crucially, the maps will also show uncertainty, helping users understand where predictions are reliable and where more measurements are needed. Rainfall, soil moisture, climate and river-flow information will then be integrated to investigate potential flood and drought hotspots.
